A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same FANTOM framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic causal-discovery experiments, wind-tunnel evaluations, and EEG seizure-detection results, including additional experiments in Appendix F.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds component ablations, standardization comparisons, expanded initialization experiments, and two-lag evaluations.

M1.justification: The structural equations, temporal graph network, conditional flows, Bayesian structure learning, and regime assignment/pruning procedure remain unchanged. The new Gaussian and spline variants are experimental ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds explicit evaluation of FANTOM in a stationary, single-regime heteroscedastic scenario in Table 4. The synthetic noise families, wind-tunnel domain, and ten-patient TUSZ evaluation remain unchanged; the other additions primarily vary experimental settings.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 introduces two evaluated comparison variants: FANTOM-Gauss without a flow and FANTOM-Spline with a simpler flow. The external baseline sets in the retained graph-learning and regime-detection comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: The initialization study expands from ten nodes and two/three regimes to ten/forty nodes and two to four regimes, including longer sequences. New protocols compare raw versus standardized data and evaluate L=2 synthetic series using a summary graph for lagged edges. These are bounded extensions of the existing evaluation; the main experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 primarily tests window-size/minimum-duration sensitivity and compares regime detectors. V2 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence with flow-component removal/replacement tests, standardization robustness against CASTOR, broader initialization/runtime analyses, and explicit larger-lag evaluation. These examine additional questions about component necessity and practical robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions state three repetitions for synthetic dataset configurations and report means with standard deviations in the detailed benchmark tables. V2's checklist reiterates this practice; the added studies introduce no new seed counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Substantial supplementary findings are added: Table 4 reports collapse to one regime for both simplified variants in the two-regime test, Table 7 provides raw/standardized results, and Table 20 supplies L=2 outcomes. The initialization study also reports revised scores and runtimes. Tables 1–3 and the benchmark results in v1 Tables 6–17, now v2 Tables 8–19, are retained. The new settings do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds the derivation connecting the ELBO to the M-step objective through fixed posterior probabilities and constant entropy. Theorem 4.3 and Appendix H.4 change the model-family indexing from K members to positive-integer indexing, although the theorem retains inconsistent 'family of K' wording. The other identifiability results and proof strategies remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: joint regime and graph discovery under non-Gaussian or heteroscedastic noise, identifiability guarantees, and empirical superiority. The added experiments support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds failure conditions involving unsuitable initialization and over-pruning, plus cautions about treating learned graphs as causal ground truth. Appendix F adds interpretations concerning conditional-flow necessity, scalability, and standardization robustness, attributing the latter to Bayesian graph learning and conditional flows.

D1.justification: V2 adds a FANTOM repository link in Section 5.1, statements about supplementary reproduction instructions, and V100-SXM2 hardware information for the additional experiments. Expanded runtime measurements also aid resource assessment. The existing architecture and optimization details in Appendix E are retained; repository accessibility is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning against previous methods are unchanged. Reference 13 updates the causal-chambers work from its preprint to its published title and venue, rather than introducing a different work.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and Section 3, subdivides Appendices C and F, expands local explanations and limitations, and appends a NeurIPS checklist. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds component, standardization, and L=2 tables, and restructures the initialization tables by node count with revised columns. It also shades selected formal statements and adjusts table placement and pagination. The existing figures are retained rather than redrawn.

improvement.justification: The component ablations and robustness tests make the design choices more assessable, while the derivation, initialization limitations, and code/hardware disclosures improve clarity and reproducibility information. The gains are qualified: the new studies lack uncertainty estimates, and the standardization discussion claims 'the same results' despite Table 7 reporting 97.1% versus 91.1% regime accuracy for two regimes. Overall, these are useful but limited improvements to a paper whose principal findings remain unchanged.
